title: Cancel Hidden Roku Add-On Channels in 3 Steps
hook_text: STOP PAYING FOR HIDDEN STREAMING CHANNELS

beats.say: You're paying for streaming add-on channels that you haven't opened since last year.
beats.visual: A dark, moody living room with a glowing flat-screen television mounted above a clean wooden credenza, casting cold blue ambient light onto an empty sofa.

beats.say: Where is that invisible cash leak quietly draining your checking account every single month?
beats.visual: A close-up shot from behind of a person sitting in shadows, holding a black remote control pointed toward a dark screen.

beats.say: Most people assume every single entertainment charge shows up inside their phone's app store.
beats.visual: A sleek smartphone resting face down on a dark granite nightstand next to a glass of water, illuminated by soft moonlight.

beats.say: That's the trap. Hardware platforms like Roku quietly bill secondary channel add-ons directly behind the scenes.
beats.visual: Macro lens view of a small black streaming box connected by HDMI cable behind a modern television set, dust motes floating in dim lighting.

beats.say: According to the math, a single $15/month subscription silently wastes $1,800 over 10 years.
beats.visual: A neat stack of paper bank statements sitting beside an unbranded ceramic coffee cup on an oak desk under a warm spotlight.

beats.say: What forgotten recurring charges are tied to your living room hardware right now?
beats.visual: A silhouette of hands typing deliberately on a slim laptop keyboard in a quiet, shadowy home office.

beats.say: Step one. Open an internet browser on your computer and log into your primary Roku account.
beats.visual: An over-the-shoulder view of a dimly lit desk, showing a person logging into a web portal on a laptop screen from a distance, screen blurred.

beats.say: Skip your television remote entirely, because physical TV menus often bury secondary third-party add-on billing.
beats.visual: A black plastic streaming remote resting abandoned on the edge of a modern coffee table, out of focus in the foreground.

beats.say: Step two. Click your user profile, select manage your subscriptions, and inspect the active list carefully.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a person's index finger clicking a metal trackpad in a calm, dimly lit workspace.

beats.say: Look for forgotten trial channels, standalone sports tiers, and movie add-ons you abandoned months ago.
beats.visual: A low-angle cinematic shot of a modern living room interior, quiet and still, with warm accent lights highlighting architectural details.

beats.say: Step three. Click turn off auto-renew on every inactive channel to stop the monthly leak immediately.
beats.visual: A neat, organized desktop workspace with a closed laptop, a brass pen, and a warm desk lamp casting clean geometric shadows.

beats.say: That simple audit saves you hundreds. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A calm, wide shot of an elegant modern apartment interior with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking a city skyline at dusk.

caption: Streaming hardware platforms bill hidden add-ons you probably forgot existed. Here is how to cancel them in 3 steps. #money #personalfinance #streaming #subscriptions #financialfreedom
description: Overlooked streaming add-ons billed through TV hardware like Roku silently drain your bank balance. Follow this 3-step audit on your web browser to eliminate unused channel subscriptions today.
first_comment: How many streaming subscriptions are you currently paying for across all devices?

facts.basis: Money fact sheet calculation: $15/month * 12 months * 10 years = $1,800.
